description: Pricing engine + single-vs-bulk classifier + market price display. Implements P0 items 9 and 10 behind clean, swappable interfaces (section 15, 16, 38). The PricingEngine computes market price, recent sold range, competition, lowest comparable, suggested price (respecting Fast Sale / Balanced / Maximum Profit modes), estimated fees, estimated shipping, and estimated net profit from seeded PriceSnapshots + deterministic math. The ClassificationService recommends SELL INDIVIDUALLY / BULK / REVIEW using a multi-factor model (value, fees, shipping, expected sell time, demand, competition, seller preferences) - NOT a fixed threshold - and returns a human-readable explanation. A dedicated Pricing page and price panels on the Card Detail page surface all of this. Global pricing preferences live in Settings.
steps: Reminder: zero deps, `unset NODE_OPTIONS`. Read FEAT-002 repositories (priceSnapshotsRepo, inventoryRepo) and card_detail view, and src/services/interfaces from FEAT-001 if present (else create the interfaces dir here).

src/services/interfaces/pricing.ts: define PricingEngine interface: getMarketData(cardId): {marketPrice, low, high, recentSoldLow, recentSoldHigh, competitionCount, lowestComparable, source, capturedAt} | null; priceCard(input:{cardId, condition, mode}): {marketPrice, suggestedPrice, estimatedFees, estimatedShipping, estimatedNet, mode, rationale}. Fees/shipping assumptions come from user settings (fee %, per-order shipping, packaging). Document that a real price-feed implementation can replace the mock without UI changes.

src/services/mock/mockPricingEngine.ts: implements PricingEngine using priceSnapshotsRepo. If a snapshot exists use it; else derive a deterministic pseudo-market value from card rarity/holo via the tcg strategy (seeded, stable). suggestedPrice adjusts by mode: Fast Sale ~ slightly below market/lowest comparable, Balanced ~ market, Maximum Profit ~ above market. Fees = salePrice * feePct (default 12.9% + $0.30) and shipping/packaging from settings; net = suggested - fees - shipping - packaging. Pure functions where possible for testability.

src/services/interfaces/classification.ts + src/services/mock/mockClassificationService.ts: ClassificationService.classify(input:{marketData, pricing, settings}): {decision:'SELL_INDIVIDUALLY'|'BULK'|'REVIEW', estimatedNet, recommendedPrice, reason} implementing a scoring model over value, net-after-fees, demand proxy (inverse of competition / recent sold volume), competition, expected sell time, and seller preference thresholds. Explicitly NOT a single fixed price cutoff: combine factors into a score with configurable weights; low net or thin margin after fees/shipping => BULK; strong net + healthy demand + low competition => SELL_INDIVIDUALLY; borderline => REVIEW. Produce the exact style of explanation shown in section 10 example (e.g. 'Estimated market value: $11.80 / Expected net after fees/shipping: $9.31 / Recommended listing price: $12.99 / Reason: Strong demand and relatively low competition.').

src/services/settings.ts + Settings page (src/views/pages/settings.ts, routes GET/POST /settings): read/write per-user pricing preferences on the users settings blob: pricingMode (Fast Sale/Balanced/Maximum Profit, section 16), fee percentage + fixed fee, default shipping cost, packaging cost, single-vs-bulk score thresholds/weights, bulk value cutoff hint. Settings drive the pricing engine + classifier.

Wire pricing into Card Detail (FEAT-002 view): add a price panel per section 15 (Market / Recommended listing / Estimated fees / Estimated shipping / Estimated net) and a classification recommendation card per section 10 (decision badge + explanation). Recompute when condition/mode change.

src/views/pages/pricing.ts + route GET /pricing: a dedicated Pricing dashboard listing inventory with market price, suggested price, net, competition, and the single-vs-bulk recommendation per row; allow switching pricing mode (persisted to settings) and see suggestions update; highlight underpriced/overpriced listings (compare listing price vs suggested) which the dashboard 'attention' section will later consume.

src/api/pricing.ts: GET /api/pricing/:cardId?condition=&mode= returns priceCard result; GET /api/classify/:inventoryId returns classify result. Used by front-end enhancement on Card Detail + Pricing pages.

Add a recompute-and-store step: when pricing an inventory item, optionally persist market_value and target_price back onto the inventory row (so Inventory/Dashboard reflect current values). Provide a bulk 'recompute values' action on the Pricing page that iterates the user's inventory.

Tests (node:test): src/services/mockPricingEngine.test.ts - deterministic outputs for known snapshots + mode variations (Fast < Balanced < MaxProfit ordering; fees/net math correct). src/services/mockClassificationService.test.ts - a $0.75 card => BULK, a $12 card with low competition => SELL_INDIVIDUALLY, a borderline ~$3 case => REVIEW or a defensible decision, and that the explanation contains the market value, expected net, and recommended price. Assert it is NOT a pure fixed-threshold (e.g. a $5 card with terrible net after huge shipping can still be BULK).
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` and `npm test` pass including pricing + classification tests.
PricingEngine returns market/suggested/fees/shipping/net and suggested price ordering respects mode (Fast Sale <= Balanced <= Maximum Profit for the same card).

ClassificationService returns SELL_INDIVIDUALLY / BULK / REVIEW from a multi-factor score (not a lone fixed threshold) with a human-readable explanation matching the section-10 format, verified by tests including the $0.75, ~$3, and $12 examples.
Card Detail shows the price panel and recommendation; the Pricing page lists inventory with prices + recommendations and lets the user change pricing mode (persisted in Settings).
Settings page reads and writes per-user pricing preferences that measurably change pricing/classification output.

findings: Implemented PricingEngine (interfaces/pricing.ts) + mockPricingEngine (seeded snapshots else deterministic rarity/holo derivation), ClassificationService (interfaces/classification.ts) + mockClassificationService (multi-factor score: net/value/demand/competition weighted, thresholds), settingsService persisting to users.pricing_mode column + settings_json.pricing blob. Removed the old stub PricingEngine/ClassificationService from interfaces/index.ts (nothing imported them) and re-exported the new types from there. New pages: /settings (GET/POST), /pricing (GET) + /pricing/mode + /pricing/recompute (writes market_value/target_price back onto all inventory rows). API: GET /api/pricing/:cardId?condition=&mode= and GET /api/classify/:inventoryId?condition=&mode=. Card Detail now shows a section-15 price panel + section-10 recommendation card that recompute live via app.js on condition/mode change. Verified: build + 43 tests pass (13 new). Live curl against seeded demo confirmed mode ordering (Charizard fast 34.64 <= balanced 43.30 <= max 48.50), classify SELL_INDIVIDUALLY vs BULK, section-10 explanation format, settings changes measurably alter fees/net, mode switch persisted, recompute updated 184 rows. Env: `unset NODE_OPTIONS` required before every node/npm/tsc; server must be started with nohup so it survives the tool-call process group. Node/npm scripts use --no-warnings for node:sqlite.
